mcqs.q: What is the difference between weather and climate?
options: Weather is short-term atmospheric conditions at a specific time and place; climate is the long-term (typically 30-year) average of weather patterns in a region.
MDGs and SDGs are the same — just renamed.
Weather refers to rain and climate refers to temperature.
Weather happens outside and climate happens globally.

mcqs.q: How are fold mountains like the Himalayas formed?
options: Fold mountains form from giant volcanoes erupting upwards.
MDGs and SDGs are the same — just renamed.
Fold mountains form when one plate slides under another into the mantle.
By the collision of two continental plates (India and Eurasia) where neither can subduct, so the crust crumples and is forced upwards over millions of years.

mcqs.q: What changed between the MDGs (Millennium Development Goals) and the SDGs (Sustainable Development Goals)?
options: MDGs (2000-2015) targeted LICs on basic poverty/health/education; SDGs (2015-2030) apply to all countries and include environmental and inequality goals — broader, more universal scope.
Weather refers to rain and climate refers to temperature.
The SDGs replaced the MDGs because the MDGs were achieved.
MDGs and SDGs are the same — just renamed.
